hints.title: Shortest Path Equivalent
hints.text: Entering a cell with 1 reduces health by 1, while entering a cell with 0 costs 0. The goal is to find a path that minimizes total health loss.

hints.title: Zero-One BFS Structure
hints.text: Because all edge weights are either 0 or 1, a double-ended queue (0-1 BFS) finds the minimum damage in linear time without priority queue overhead.

hints.title: Health Condition
hints.text: Health must remain at least 1 upon reaching (m-1, n-1), which means total health loss from start to target must be strictly less than initial health.

hints.title: Reference Implementation

complexity.notes: 0-1 BFS visits each cell at most a constant number of times.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Standard DFS backtracks over exponential paths without visiting order optimality.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Distance table and deque require O(m * n) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Models grid traversal as 0-1 BFS shortest path to minimize damage.
